articles.title: Understanding your bill and the incentives in Mauritius
articles.excerpt: Baseline consumption, kilowatt-hours, local incentives: we strip out the jargon to show you what actually matters.

sections.heading: What your bill doesn't tell you
body: An electricity bill lists kilowatt-hours and standing charges, but it never says what's actually driving your costs up: the afternoon AC, the rice cooker, the water heater running non-stop.
We'd rather start from your daily routine than your meter reading: which appliances, at what times, for what use.

sections.heading: The incentives available, without making them the headline
body: Local incentives can fund part of your installation and buy back your surplus production for 20 years. These schemes are real, but they don't replace a system sized around your actual usage.
We walk you through what applies to your situation before ever talking about equipment — never the other way round.

sections.heading: A concrete example
body: A household paying €150/month can, depending on its consumption profile, drop to around €22/month once equipped — an average of €30,000 saved over 20 years. Every household is different, which is exactly why we study yours specifically.

articles.title: How to properly compare two solar quotes
articles.excerpt: Two quotes, two prices, two different promises. Here are the questions to ask before signing anything.

sections.heading: Price alone tells you nothing
body: A cheaper quote can hide a system sized to your roof's surface area rather than your real consumption — you produce, but you don't consume what you produce.
Always ask: what basis was the power output calculated on?

sections.heading: The questions to ask every time
body: Is the equipment certified to withstand cyclone season? What's the actual length of the warranty, and what exactly does it cover? Who stays reachable after installation, and within what timeframe?
A serious installer answers these questions clearly, without deflecting to "government incentives" as the only argument.

sections.heading: The right reflex
body: Put both quotes side by side and compare line by line: installed power, storage offered, warranties, response time in case of a fault. If a point stays unclear, that's the moment to ask — not after you've signed.

faq.pageDescription: Cyclones, your roof, incentives, resale: real answers to the questions we actually get asked, before you sign anything.

items.question: Why install solar panels now in Mauritius?
items.answer: Your electricity bill keeps rising year after year. Installing now protects you from those increases for the next 25 years, while today's incentives remain advantageous — they can change.

items.question: How much can you really save?
items.answer: It depends on your consumption, the type of installation and your habits. Some Mauritian households cut their bill by more than 80%. The savings are even greater when you consume the electricity you produce directly, unlike a standard bill that keeps rising every year.

items.question: Does it still produce on a cloudy day?
items.answer: Yes. Panels also capture diffuse light, even behind clouds. In Mauritius, even during the rainy season, sunlight remains largely sufficient to keep meaningful production going. A storage battery becomes useful for the truly sunless days.

items.question: What happens during a cyclone?
items.answer: During a cyclone, the power grid can go down for several hours, sometimes several days. Paired with a storage battery, your installation keeps the essentials running.

items.question: Can I keep the energy I produce?
items.answer: Yes. A storage battery keeps the electricity produced during the day for use in the evening or at night. Any surplus can be resold under the terms in force.

items.question: My roof is small — is it still possible?
items.answer: Usually, yes. High-efficiency panels maximise production on a limited surface. Solutions are sized around your real consumption, not your roof size.

items.question: Will the installation damage my roof?
items.answer: No. Our teams use certified fixing systems, adapted to every type of roof. A professional installation prevents leaks and damage.

items.question: How long does it actually take?
items.answer: The installation itself is usually done in a single day. Administrative timelines vary, but we handle the entire process for you.

items.question: Does a solar installation add value to my home?
items.answer: Yes. An equipped home consumes less and produces its own energy, which appeals to buyers. Given how much electricity bills weigh on a household budget, that's a real selling point on the market.

items.question: What if I produce more than I consume?
items.answer: The surplus electricity can be resold under the terms in force, creating extra income on top of your bill savings.

items.question: Do I need to handle any administrative steps?
items.answer: Registering with the electricity provider is one of the administrative steps we handle entirely for you.

items.question: What incentives are available in Mauritius?
items.answer: Local incentives exist to support residents in their solar transition. They change regularly depending on current regulations — we tell you exactly what applies to your situation before we ever talk about equipment.

items.question: I've had bad experiences before — why should I trust you?
items.answer: One Énergie is a local team, by your side before, during and after the installation — with no pushy sales tactics. You'll always deal with someone who knows the island and its specifics, not a stranger passing through.
